name: What causes ADU bathroom construction to go over budget?

mainEntity.name: Which hidden issues usually make an ADU bathroom more expensive than the original estimate?
mainEntity.text: Which hidden issues usually make an ADU bathroom more expensive than the original estimate?

acceptedAnswer.text: ADU bathroom budgets go over more often because of hidden plumbing and structural conditions than because of fixtures. A long drain route, an unexpected sewer tie-in problem, slab cutting, or a need to reroute vents can quickly add labor and materials. Waterproofing upgrades, custom tile work, glass enclosures, and higher-end finishes also raise the price, but those are usually visible from the start. The biggest surprise is often an unknown condition behind the existing walls or under the slab, such as damaged piping, undersized drains, or a route that does not have enough slope. Permit corrections and design revisions can also add time and cost. To reduce risk, homeowners should ask for a line-item estimate, confirm fixture locations early, and have the contractor explain exactly how the bathroom will connect to water, waste, and venting. In ADU work, the cheapest-looking bathroom design is not always the least expensive once the plumbing is fully solved. A simple layout with a short plumbing run is usually the most reliable budget choice.
acceptedAnswer.description: The biggest budget overruns usually come from long plumbing runs, slab cutting, sewer tie-ins, waterproofing changes, tile upgrades, ventilation fixes, and permit revisions. Unknown conditions behind walls or under concrete can also trigger change orders. Bathroom budgets stay more stable when the plumbing plan is solved before construction begins.
